mainTopic: The dead and their honor, נידוי for disrespecting תלמידי חכמים, and קריאת שמע at a funeral.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a proof that the dead know what happens in this world. The proof rests on the word 'לאמר', read as ה׳ telling משה to go inform the אבות, and the telling turns out to give credit to משה. Next, רבי יצחק says that speaking badly of the dead is like speaking about a stone. The גמרא answers a challenge to this: a תלמיד חכם is different, because הקדוש ברוך הוא guards his honor. That leads to teachings on כבוד תלמידי חכמים: insulting a dead scholar leads to גיהנם, and a scholar seen sinning is assumed to have done תשובה, unless the sin involved someone else's money. רבי יהושע בן לוי then says there are 24 cases of נידוי for a רב's honor in the משנה. רבי אלעזר finds only three: עקביא בן מהללאל, אלעזר בן חנוך, and חוני המעגל. The challenges from תודוס and the oven of עכנאי are answered. The difference is that רבי יהושע בן לוי reasons by comparing similar cases and רבי אלעזר does not. Finally the גמרא returns to the funeral laws of our משנה: when to take out the מת near קריאת שמע, how eulogizers and the mourner act, אביי's warning not to 'open your mouth to the שטן', and how much of שמע people returning from a burial must be able to finish.

steps.title: The verse only makes sense if the dead know
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא presses its proof from the verse: if the dead knew nothing, telling the אבות anything would be pointless.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think that the dead do not know anything, then what is accomplished when He tells them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its proof that the dead know what happens in this world. It uses the verse in which ה׳ tells משה to go and tell the אבות that the oath was kept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says 'לאמר' ('saying'), which is read as 'go tell the אבות.' The logic is simple: you only bother telling someone something if they can know it. So the verse seems to show that the dead are aware.

keyTerms.meaning: If it should enter your mind (if you were to think)
They know (here: the dead are aware)
What would it accomplish? What difference does it make?

steps.confusionAlert: This step depends on the verse quoted on the previous amud: 'זאת הארץ אשר נשבעתי לאברהם ליצחק וליעקב לאמר.' The whole argument rests on reading 'לאמר' as 'go tell them.'

phrases.english: And if it should enter your mind
that they (the dead) do not know,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the dead, here the אבות.

phrases.english: when He tells them, what does it accomplish?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof from the verse, which was quoted on the previous amud.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the dead know what happens in this world.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים לד:ד, 'לאמר' read as 'go tell the אבות.'

steps.title: If they already know, why tell them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the logic around: if the dead do know, there should be no need to tell them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what do you want to say, that they do know? Then why does He need to tell them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes a hole in the proof. If the dead already know everything, telling them would also be unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof argued that telling them makes sense only if they can know. But if they really know, then telling them adds nothing either. So the verse now seems puzzling under both possibilities.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what [will you say]? (a turnaround question)

phrases.english: Rather, what — that they know?
Why does He need to tell them?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof in step 1 by showing that 'they know' also makes telling them seem pointless.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from 'לאמר' that the dead know.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the dead already know, the instruction to tell them is unnecessary. So the verse cannot simply be explained by 'they know.'

steps.title: Telling them gives credit to משה
steps.stepSummary: The answer: they do know, but the telling is meant to make them appreciate משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The purpose of telling them is so that they will feel gratitude toward משה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of why the dead need to be told. The point of the message is to give משה credit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the אבות know what happens, the message has a new purpose. It credits משה as the one through whom the promise came true. So the verse fits the view that the dead know.

keyTerms.meaning: To cause to hold, to give (credit)

steps.whatToRemember: The verse 'לאמר' is used to show that the dead know. The telling is not to inform them, but to credit משה.

phrases.english: So that they will give credit (gratitude) to Moses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the purpose of the telling: it gives credit rather than information.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Telling the dead only makes sense as giving them new information.
steps.terutzMaskana: The telling serves to honor משה. So the verse still fits the view that the dead know.

steps.title: Speaking about the dead is like speaking about a stone
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that speaking badly about someone who has died is like speaking about a stone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: Anyone who speaks badly about a dead person, it is as if he is speaking about a stone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching on the same topic of what the dead know. רבי יצחק compares the dead to a stone when people speak against them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison to a stone means that speaking against the dead does not affect them. But it is not yet clear why: is it because they do not know, or for some other reason? The next step explains this.

keyTerms.meaning: One who speaks behind / after (badly about)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Anyone who speaks (negatively) after the dead,
it is as if he speaks after the stone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new, related teaching on whether the dead are aware of the living.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Speaking against the dead does not affect them, just as speaking about a stone does not affect the stone.

steps.title: Two explanations of the stone comparison
steps.stepSummary: Two explanations: either the dead do not know, or they know but do not care.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say this is because the dead do not know. And some say they do know, but it does not bother them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the dead are compared to a stone, giving two different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view says the dead are simply unaware, like a stone. The second view says they are aware but do not care. Both views agree on the result: the insult does not bother the dead.

keyTerms.meaning: It does not matter to them; they do not care

phrases.english: Some say that they do not know,
and some say that they know
but it does not matter to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רבי יצחק's comparison in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dead are not affected by insults, either because they do not know or because they do not care.

steps.title: The story of the man who insulted שמואל
steps.stepSummary: A challenge from רב פפא's story: a man spoke against שמואל after his death, and a reed fell and cracked his skull.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? Didn't רב פפא say: One person spoke badly about מר שמואל after he died, and a reed fell from the roof and cracked his skull?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יצחק. It brings a story showing that insulting a dead person did have a result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the dead do not know or do not care, why was this man punished right away? The story suggests that the dead, or Heaven, do care about insults against the dead. This attacks both explanations from step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'pouch' of his brain, his skull

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't Rav Pappa say:
One person spoke a (disparaging) word
after (the death of) Mar Shmuel
and a reed fell from the roof
and split open his skull!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יצחק's teaching from steps 4 and 5 with a story.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's claim that speaking against the dead is like speaking against a stone.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The immediate punishment shows that insulting the dead matters. That seems to contradict 'they do not know' and 'they do not care.'

steps.title: A Torah scholar is different
steps.stepSummary: The answer: a תלמיד חכם is different, because הקדוש ברוך הוא Himself protects his honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תלמיד חכם is different, because הקדוש ברוך הוא Himself demands that his honor be protected.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. שמואל's case was special because he was a תלמיד חכם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The punishment did not come because the dead שמואל cared. It came because ה׳ defends the honor of a תלמיד חכם. So רבי יצחק's general rule still stands, and a תלמיד חכם is an exception.

keyTerms.meaning: A תלמיד חכם, a Torah scholar
The Holy One, Blessed is He

steps.whatToRemember: Speaking against the dead does not harm them, according to רבי יצחק. But insulting a dead תלמיד חכם brings punishment, because ה׳ Himself guards his honor.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches the special severity of disrespecting a תלמיד חכם, even after his death.

phrases.english: A Torah scholar is different,
for the Holy One, Blessed be He, demands (upholds) his honor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רב פפא's story in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the case: a תלמיד חכם is a special exception.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The punishment shows that the dead care when they are insulted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The punishment came from ה׳'s concern for a תלמיד חכם's honor. It does not show that the dead care, so רבי יצחק's rule remains.

steps.title: Speaking against dead תלמידי חכמים leads to גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that whoever speaks badly about תלמידי חכמים after their death falls into גיהנם. He brings a פסוק from תהלים as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Anyone who speaks badly about תלמידי חכמים after they have died falls into גיהנם. The פסוק says: 'Those who turn to their crooked ways, ה׳ will lead them away with the workers of evil; peace upon Israel.' This means that even at a time when there is peace upon Israel, ה׳ will still lead them away with the workers of evil.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives a strong new rule: speaking badly about a dead תלמיד חכם is punished with גיהנם. He supports it with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the last step, which said that הקדוש ברוך הוא Himself protects a תלמיד חכם's honor. The word 'וְהַמַּטִּים' is read as a hint to 'מִטָּתָן', the bier of the dead. 'Peace upon Israel' is read as a time when the scholar can no longer defend himself, and even then the speaker is punished.

keyTerms.meaning: One who speaks against them after their bier (after their death)
גיהנם, the place of punishment after death

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how seriously the גמרא treats the honor of a תלמיד חכם. That honor continues even after he has died.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Anyone who speaks (badly) after the biers
phrases.notes: In other words, after they have died.

phrases.english: of Torah scholars
falls into Gehinnom,
as it says: 'But those who turn aside to their crooked ways,'
phrases.notes: תהלים קכ״ה:ה. The word 'המטים' hints at 'מטה', a bier.

phrases.english: ה׳ will lead them away with the workers of evil;
peace upon Israel.'
Even at a time when there is peace upon Israel,
phrases.notes: Meaning after the scholar's death, when he can no longer fight back.

phrases.english: 'ה׳ will lead them away with the workers of evil.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: כׇּל הַמְסַפֵּר אַחַר מִטָּתָן שֶׁל תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a punishment, based on a פסוק, to the idea that הקדוש ברוך הוא protects the honor of a תלמיד חכם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Speaking badly about a תלמיד חכם after his death leads to גיהנם.

steps.title: Do not think badly of a scholar who sinned at night
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל says: if you saw a תלמיד חכם sin at night, do not suspect him the next day, because perhaps he did תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: If you saw a תלמיד חכם commit a sin at night, do not think badly of him the next day. Perhaps he has done תשובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related teaching about the honor of תלמידי חכמים. You must judge a scholar favorably even after seeing him sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps were about not speaking badly about scholars. This step goes further: you should not even think badly of them. The reason given is that he may already have done תשובה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל (a ברייתא)
Do not think (suspicious) thoughts about him

phrases.english: It was taught in the school of Rabbi Yishmael:
If you saw a Torah scholar
who committed a sin at night,
do not think badly of him during the day,
since perhaps he has repented.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: אִם רָאִיתָ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁעָבַר עֲבֵירָה בַּלַּיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the theme of כבוד תלמידי חכמים from speech to thought.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not suspect a תלמיד חכם the day after seeing him sin, because he may have done תשובה.

steps.title: Is it really only 'perhaps'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the word 'שמא' (perhaps). Can it be that he only maybe repented?
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think it is only 'perhaps'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to one word in the ברייתא. The word 'perhaps' sounds too weak for a תלמיד חכם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is on the wording, not on the rule itself. A תלמיד חכם deserves more than 'maybe he repented'. The step is setting up the correction that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Would it enter your mind? (Can you really think so?)

phrases.english: 'Perhaps'? Would that enter your mind?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'שמא' in the ברייתא of דבי רבי ישמעאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תלמיד חכם who sinned surely regrets it, so saying 'perhaps' understates his righteousness.

steps.title: He certainly repented
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the wording: the scholar has certainly done תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he certainly repented.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own challenge by upgrading 'perhaps' to 'certainly'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the reason not to suspect him was only a possibility. Now it is a firm assumption that a תלמיד חכם does תשובה for his sins. This makes the obligation to judge him favorably stronger.

phrases.english: Rather, he certainly repented.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the wording challenge.
steps.terutzMaskana: We assume for certain that the scholar repented.

steps.title: The rule applies only to personal sins, not money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the rule. It applies only to sins that involve himself. If the sin involves someone else's money, we do not assume he repented until he returns it to its owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only to sins that involve his own body. But with money, we do not assume he repented until he gives it back to its owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to the rule it just made. Judging the scholar favorably works for personal sins, but not for sins involving someone else's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תשובה for a personal sin happens inside a person, so we can assume it happened. When money was taken from another person, תשובה requires returning it. So until the money goes back, we cannot assume he repented.

keyTerms.meaning: And these words (apply only)... introduces a limitation
Until he returns it to its owner

steps.whatToRemember: We assume a תלמיד חכם has done תשובה for personal sins. For money sins, we wait until he returns what he took.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean a תלמיד חכם cannot do תשובה for money sins. It only means his תשובה requires returning the money, so we cannot assume it until we see that happen.

phrases.english: And this applies only to matters involving himself.
But with money (of others),
not until he returns it to its owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule established in steps 9–11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The assumption of תשובה applies to personal sins. For monetary sins, it applies only once the money is returned.

steps.title: Twenty-four cases of excommunication for a rabbi's honor
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that in 24 places בית דין puts a person in נידוי for disrespecting a רב, and all of them are in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי also said: In 24 places, בית דין puts someone in נידוי for the honor of the רב, and we learned all of them in our משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching on the same theme of honoring Torah scholars. This one is about the court's power to punish disrespect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the punishment for disrespect came from Heaven (גיהנם). Here we learn that an earthly court also acts, with נידוי. The claim that all 24 cases are in the משנה sets up the question that comes next.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
In twenty-four places

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית דִּין מְנַדִּין עַל כְּבוֹד הָרַב,
phrases.english: the court excommunicates for the honor of the rabbi,
and we learned all of them in our Mishnah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה מְקוֹמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching by the same אמורא on the same theme of כבוד תלמידי חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are 24 cases in the משנה where בית דין excommunicates for disrespect of a רב.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר asks where they are
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks רבי יהושע בן לוי where in the משנה these 24 cases are found.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said to him: Where?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר asks for the sources behind the claim. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר is not disagreeing. He simply wants to know where in the משנה the cases are, since they are not obvious.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said to him: Where?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Requests the sources for the claim in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The locations in the משנה of the 24 cases of נידוי.

steps.title: Go and you will find them
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי does not list the cases. He tells רבי אלעזר that if he looks, he will find them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: When you go look, you will find them.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of listing the cases, רבי יהושע בן לוי tells רבי אלעזר to search for them himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer gives no information. It sends the student to do his own work, and that sets up the next step, where רבי אלעזר actually searches.

phrases.english: He said to him: When you look, you will find.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי אלעזר's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No list is given. The student is told to search the משנה himself.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר searches and finds three
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר went out, examined the משנה, and found three cases: one who belittles נטילת ידים, one who speaks badly about dead תלמידי חכמים, and one who is arrogant toward Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went out, looked carefully, and found three: one who belittles washing the hands, one who speaks badly after the bier of תלמידי חכמים, and one who acts arrogantly toward Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר does the search and reports what he found. He finds three of the 24 cases, and the גמרא will next bring the sources for each.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The search turns up only three, not all 24. The second case connects directly back to step 8, where speaking against dead scholars was punished with גיהנם. Now we learn it also brings נידוי from בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: He went out and examined carefully
One who acts arrogantly toward Heaven

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר found three cases of נידוי in the משנה: belittling נטילת ידים, speaking against dead תלמידי חכמים, and arrogance toward Heaven.

phrases.english: He went out, examined, and found three:
one who belittles the washing of hands,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַמְסַפֵּר אַחַר מִטָּתָן שֶׁל תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים,
phrases.english: and one who speaks (badly) after the biers of Torah scholars,
and one who is arrogant toward Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the search prompted in step 15 and partly answers step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three of the 24 cases: belittling נטילת ידים, speaking against dead scholars, and arrogance toward Heaven.

steps.title: Where is the case of speaking badly about dead scholars?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where in the משנה we find נידוי for someone who speaks badly about תלמידי חכמים after they died.
steps.simpleTranslation: "One who speaks badly after the biers of תלמידי חכמים": what case is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the first of רבי אלעזר's three cases and asks where it appears in the משנה. This question sets up the next step, where the source will be quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר named three cases but did not quote their sources. Now the גמרא goes back and asks for the actual משנה behind each one, starting with speaking badly about dead scholars.

keyTerms.meaning: Their bier, the bed on which the dead are carried. Here it means after their death.
What is it? A request to identify the source.

phrases.english: "One who speaks [badly] after the biers of Torah scholars"
phrases.notes: Quoting the case רבי אלעזר found

phrases.english: what is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the משנה source of one of the three cases listed in Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The משנה source showing נידוי for speaking badly about dead תלמידי חכמים.

steps.title: עקביא בן מהללאל and the story of כרכמית
steps.stepSummary: The משנה about סוטה: עקביא בן מהללאל said שמעיה and אבטליון made the freed maidservant drink only because she was like them. For this he was put in נידוי, and when he died his coffin was stoned.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: He [עקביא בן מהללאל] used to say: We do not give the bitter waters to a convert or to a freed maidservant. The חכמים say: We do give it to them. They said to him: There was a case with כרכמית, a freed maidservant in ירושלים, and שמעיה and אבטליון gave her the waters to drink! He answered them: They made her drink because she was like them. So they put him in נידוי, he died while still in נידוי, and the בית דין stoned his coffin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a משנה. In it, עקביא בן מהללאל spoke disrespectfully about the great sages שמעיה and אבטליון, who had already died, and was put in נידוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים brought proof from a real case that שמעיה and אבטליון performed. עקביא brushed it aside by saying they only did it because she was "like them," since they also came from converts. Speaking this way about dead scholars earned him נידוי, which proves this case is one of the 24.

keyTerms.meaning: We give to drink. Here it means giving the bitter waters of a סוטה.
Like them, someone similar. A hint that שמעיה and אבטליון also came from converts.
They stoned his coffin, a sign that he died in נידוי

steps.confusionAlert: The problem was not that עקביא disagreed with the חכמים about the law. That kind of disagreement is normal. The problem was how he explained away what שמעיה and אבטליון did, which belittled dead sages.

phrases.english: As we learned: He would say:
phrases.notes: "He" is עקביא בן מהללאל

phrases.english: We do not give [the bitter waters] to drink, neither to a convert,
nor to a freed maidservant.
And the Sages say: We do give them to drink.
And they said to him: There was a case with Kharkemit,
a freed maidservant in Jerusalem,
and Shemaya and Avtalyon gave her to drink!
And he said to them: They gave her to drink because she was like them.
phrases.notes: A disrespectful remark about the dead sages

phrases.english: And they put him in נידוי, and he died in his נידוי,
and the court stoned his coffin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 17 by quoting the משנה source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה of עקביא בן מהללאל, who was put in נידוי for belittling שמעיה and אבטליון after their deaths.

steps.title: Where is the case of belittling hand-washing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where in the משנה we find נידוי for someone who belittles נטילת ידים.
steps.simpleTranslation: "One who belittles נטילת ידים": what case is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second case and asks for its source. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the first case. The גמרא names the case and asks "מאי היא" to find the משנה behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: One who belittles or treats something lightly
Ritual washing of the hands, a rabbinic enactment

phrases.english: "And one who belittles the washing of hands"
what is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second case from Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The משנה source showing נידוי for belittling נטילת ידים.

steps.title: אלעזר בן חנוך was put in נידוי for doubting hand-washing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that עקביא בן מהללאל was never put in נידוי. Rather, the one put in נידוי was אלעזר בן חנוך, who doubted נטילת ידים. When he died, a large stone was placed on his coffin.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned, רבי יהודה said: Heaven forbid that עקביא בן מהללאל was put in נידוי! Even when the עזרה was closed because it was full of all of Israel, there was no one there as great in wisdom, purity, and fear of sin as עקביא בן מהללאל. So whom did they put in נידוי? אלעזר בן חנוך, who doubted נטילת ידים. When he died, the בית דין sent and placed a large stone on his coffin. This teaches you that anyone who is in נידוי and dies in his נידוי, the בית דין stones his coffin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the continuation of the same משנה. רבי יהודה disagrees about who was put in נידוי, and in his version it was אלעזר בן חנוך, for belittling נטילת ידים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה cannot accept that a person as righteous as עקביא was put in נידוי. Instead he tells of אלעזר בן חנוך, who was put in נידוי for doubting the rabbinic law of hand-washing. This gives us the second case of the 24, and it also teaches the rule about stoning the coffin of someone who dies in נידוי.

keyTerms.meaning: The courtyard of the בית המקדש
He doubted or cast doubt on something

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how seriously חז"ל treated even a rabbinic law like נטילת ידים. Doubting it was considered disrespect for the חכמים who made it.

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: חַס וְשָׁלוֹם שֶׁעֲקַבְיָא בֶּן מַהֲלַלְאֵל נִתְנַדָּה,
phrases.english: Heaven forbid that Akavya ben Mahalalel was put in נידוי,
for the Temple courtyard was not closed
on any person in Israel
in wisdom, in purity, and in fear of sin
like Akavya ben Mahalalel.
phrases.notes: In other words, no one was as great as he was

phrases.english: Rather, whom did they put in נידוי?
Elazar ben Chanokh,
who cast doubt on the washing of hands.
And when he died, the court sent [messengers]
and they placed a large stone on his coffin,
to teach you that anyone who is put in נידוי
and dies in his נידוי,
the court stones his coffin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19 by quoting the continuation of the same משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה's statement that אלעזר בן חנוך was put in נידוי for doubting נטילת ידים.

steps.title: Where is the case of arrogance toward Heaven?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where in the משנה we find נידוי for someone who acts arrogantly toward Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: "One who is arrogant toward Above": what case is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the third case and asks for its source. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the last of רבי אלעזר's three cases. The pattern is the same: name the case, then ask where it comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Toward Above, meaning toward Heaven, toward ה׳

phrases.english: "One who is arrogant toward Above"
what is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the third case from Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The משנה source showing נידוי for being arrogant toward Heaven.

steps.title: שמעון בן שטח's message to חוני המעגל
steps.stepSummary: שמעון בן שטח told חוני המעגל that he deserved נידוי for the bold way he demanded rain. But since ה׳ treats חוני like a beloved son, שמעון בן שטח did not put him in נידוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: שמעון בן שטח sent a message to חוני המעגל: You deserve to be put in נידוי. If you were not חוני, I would decree נידוי on you. But what can I do? You nag before ה׳ and He does what you want, like a son who nags his father and his father does what he wants. About you the פסוק says: "Your father and mother will rejoice, and she who gave birth to you will be glad."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה about חוני המעגל, who prayed for rain and made demands about exactly how it should fall. שמעון בן שטח said that this kind of behavior normally deserves נידוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חוני was not actually put in נידוי, but שמעון בן שטח said plainly, "צריך אתה להתנדות": you deserve it. That statement is enough to show that being arrogant toward Heaven is a case for נידוי. חוני was spared only because of his special closeness to ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: Nags or pleads like a spoiled child

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this case fails because חוני was never actually put in נידוי. The point is that his behavior deserved נידוי. Only his unique status saved him.
steps.whatToRemember: The three cases are: speaking badly about dead scholars (עקביא), belittling נטילת ידים (אלעזר בן חנוך), and arrogance toward Heaven (חוני המעגל).

phrases.aramaic: — דִּתְנַן, שָׁלַח לוֹ שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שֶׁטַח
phrases.english: As we learned: Shimon ben Shatach sent to him,
to Choni the Circle-Drawer:
You deserve to be put in נידוי,
and if you were not Choni,
I would decree נידוי upon you,
but what can I do,
since you nag before God
and He does your will for you,
like a son who nags before his father
and he does his will for him.
And about you the verse says:
"Your father and your mother will rejoice,
and she who bore you will be glad."
phrases.notes: משלי כג:כה

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן, שָׁלַח לוֹ שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שֶׁטַח לְחוֹנִי הַמְעַגֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 21 and completes the list of three sources.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה where שמעון בן שטח told חוני המעגל that he deserved נידוי for being arrogant toward Heaven.

steps.title: Are there no more cases? The story of תודוס איש רומי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the count of only three: there is another case, taught by רב יוסף, where שמעון בן שטח threatened נידוי on תודוס for having roasted young goats eaten on the night of פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are there no more? But there is the case רב יוסף taught: תודוס of Rome led the Jews of Rome to eat whole roasted young goats on the nights of פסח. שמעון בן שטח sent him a message: If you were not תודוס, I would decree נידוי on you, because you are feeding Israel קדשים outside the בית המקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי אלעזר found only three cases. It brings another case of נידוי: תודוס איש רומי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תודוס had people eat goats roasted whole, in the same style as the קרבן פסח. That made it look as if they were eating קדשים outside the בית המקדש. Since שמעון בן שטח said this deserved נידוי, it seems to be a fourth case that should have been counted.

keyTerms.meaning: Young goats roasted whole, the way the קרבן פסח was roasted
Sacred meat eaten outside the בית המקדש

phrases.english: And are there no more?
But surely there is what Rav Yosef taught:
Theodosius of Rome
instituted a custom for the people of Rome
to feed them whole-roasted young goats
on the nights of Pesach.
Shimon ben Shatach sent to him:
If you were not Theodosius,
I would decree נידוי upon you,
because you are feeding Israel
sacred food outside [the Temple].

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ לֵיכָּא? וְהָא אִיכָּא דְּתָנֵי רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the three sources are shown, the גמרא challenges the claim that only three were found.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's finding of only three cases of נידוי for disrespect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יוסף's teaching shows another case, תודוס, where שמעון בן שטח said נידוי was deserved. So why was it not counted?

steps.title: The story of תודוס does not count because it is only a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יהושע בן לוי's count covers only cases in our משנה, and the תודוס story comes from a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We said the cases are found 'in our משנה.' This story is a ברייתא, so it does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 23. The תודוס case is not part of the count because it is not in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי's original statement was limited to 'our משנה.' The תודוס story is a real case of threatened נידוי. It simply comes from a different source, a ברייתא, so it falls outside the list.

keyTerms.meaning: In our משנה, meaning the official collection of רבי יהודה הנשיא
A teaching of the תנאים that was left out of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying that תודוס was never threatened with נידוי. It is only saying that this case does not belong on the list, because the list counts only what appears in the משנה.

phrases.english: We said 'in our Mishnah.'
phrases.notes: This refers back to רבי יהושע בן לוי's wording.

phrases.english: And this one is a baraita.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the statement to a specific source, the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The list should include every known case of נידוי, so תודוס should be on it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list includes only cases in the משנה, and the תודוס story is from a ברייתא.

steps.title: Challenge from the oven of עכנאי in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer by pointing to a משנה about the oven cut into rings, the dispute between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really no other case in the משנה? There is the משנה that says: if someone cut an oven into rings and put sand between the rings, רבי אליעזר says it is pure and the חכמים say it is impure. This is the oven of עכנאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 24. Here is a case that is in the משנה, so it should have been counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 24 depended on the list covering only the משנה. Now the גמרא points to a משנה whose story, as the next steps will show, ended in נידוי. If so, the count is again too small.

keyTerms.meaning: Rings or segments; here, an oven cut sideways into pieces
Rules it pure, meaning it cannot become טמא
Rule it impure, meaning it can become טמא
The oven of עכנאי, a famous dispute

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the famous oven of עכנאי. It is the background to the well-known story in בבא מציעא about following the majority of the חכמים.

phrases.english: And in the Mishnah there are none?
But there is that which we learned:
If he cut it (an earthenware oven) into rings
and put sand between one ring and the next —
Rabbi Eliezer deems it pure,
phrases.notes: He holds that it counts as broken pieces, not a whole vessel.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis deem it impure.
phrases.notes: They hold that it still works as an oven, so it counts as a whole vessel.

phrases.english: And this is the oven of akhnai.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְמַתְנִיתִין לֵיכָּא? וְהָא אִיכָּא הָא דִתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that only cases in the משנה are counted, and that the count therefore stands.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Here is a משנה whose case involved נידוי, yet it is not on the list.

steps.title: What does עכנאי mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pauses to ask what the name עכנאי means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'עכנאי'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a side question about the strange name of the oven. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before finishing the challenge, the גמרא explains the name. As the answer shows, the name itself hints at how the dispute ended.

phrases.english: What is 'akhnai'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in the משנה quoted in Step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the name עכנאי.

steps.title: The חכמים surrounded the oven with halachic proofs like a snake
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, explains that the חכמים surrounded the oven with הלכות like a coiled snake and declared it impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the name teaches that the חכמים surrounded it with הלכות, the way a snake coils around, and declared it impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about the name. 'עכנאי' means snake, because the חכמים closed in on רבי אליעזר's ruling from every side with proofs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name is a picture of the argument. The חכמים piled up proofs around the oven, like a snake wrapping around its prey, and ruled it טמא. This shows the debate was intense and ended in a firm ruling against רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
It teaches that they surrounded it with halakhot
like this snake,
and declared it impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהִקִּיפוּהוּ הֲלָכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עכנאי means snake: the חכמים surrounded the oven with הלכות like a coiled snake and declared it impure.

steps.title: ברייתא: רבי אליעזר's pure items were burned and he was 'blessed'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reports that the items רבי אליעזר had declared pure were burned in front of him, and in the end he was 'blessed,' meaning put in נידוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: on that day they brought all the items that רבי אליעזר had declared pure and burned them in front of him. In the end, they 'blessed' him, meaning they put him in נידוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to complete its challenge. It shows that the dispute in this משנה really did end in נידוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה itself mentions only the dispute. The ברייתא proves that רבי אליעזר was actually put in נידוי over it. So a case of נידוי connected to a משנה seems to be missing from רבי יהושע בן לוי's count.

keyTerms.meaning: Pure food items, which must be kept from טומאה
They 'blessed' him, a polite way of saying they put him in נידוי

steps.confusionAlert: 'בֵּרְכוּהוּ' does not mean they gave him a blessing. It is a polite way of saying the opposite: they placed him in נידוי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This completes the challenge from the oven of עכנאי. The גמרא answers it in the very next step: the נידוי itself is not taught in the משנה.

phrases.english: And it was taught in a baraita:
On that day they brought
all the pure items that Rabbi Eliezer had declared pure
and burned them in front of him,
and in the end they 'blessed' him (put him in נידוי).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side explanation of the name to complete the קשיא of Step 25.
steps.raayaObject: That the case of the oven of עכנאי ended in נידוי, so it challenges the count.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא describing the burning of the pure items and the 'blessing' (נידוי) of רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: The נידוי itself is not in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends its earlier answer. The oven case does appear in a משנה, but the נידוי of רבי אליעזר does not. It is only reported in a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, we did not learn about the נידוי in the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the oven of עכנאי. Yes, that argument is in a משנה, but the fact that רבי אליעזר was put in נידוי is only told in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge said: here is a משנה connected to a famous נידוי, so why isn't it on the list? The answer separates the two pieces. The disagreement is in the משנה, but the נידוי itself is not. So the earlier rule still holds: the count includes only cases where the משנה itself is the source.

keyTerms.meaning: A ban or ostracism imposed by בית דין
We did not learn (it in a משנה)

phrases.english: Even so,
we did not learn the ostracism in the Mishnah.
phrases.notes: The נידוי appears only in the ברייתא cited in Step 28.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי, נִדּוּי בְּמַתְנִיתִין לָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the עכנאי case (Steps 25-28). Step 28 had shown that the נידוי is found only in a ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the source: the topic is in a משנה, but the נידוי itself is not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the oven case is in a משנה, it should count among the cases of נידוי found in a משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the halachic argument is in the משנה. The נידוי is in a ברייתא, so it is not counted.

steps.title: Then where do the 24 cases come from?
steps.stepSummary: If only explicit משנה cases count, the גמרא asks how רבי יהושע בן לוי could find as many as 24 places.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, the 'twenty-four places' — where do you find them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem. If we only count cases where a משנה clearly mentions נידוי, there are very few, so how did רבי יהושע בן לוי reach 24?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier defense made the count very strict. It is so strict that the number 24 now seems impossible. Only a few explicit cases are known, like the three רבי אלעזר found. This sets up the next step.

phrases.english: But then, "in twenty-four places" —
where do you find it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה מְקוֹמוֹת הֵיכָא מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Grows out of the strict rule set in Step 29 and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's claim of 24 places
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If only explicit משנה cases count, there are far fewer than 24.

steps.title: One Sage compares similar cases, the other does not
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי reaches 24 by comparing similar cases. רבי אלעזר counts only cases where the text clearly says נידוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי compares one matter to another, and רבי אלעזר does not compare one matter to another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the difference between the two counts. רבי יהושע בן לוי counts any משנה where a Sage spoke disrespectfully, while רבי אלעזר counts only the explicit cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are many places in the משנה where a Sage spoke improperly about other Sages. רבי יהושע בן לוי treats them like the explicit cases and concludes that נידוי was deserved there too, which gives 24. רבי אלעזר does not stretch the cases, so he finds only three.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares one matter to another (reasons by analogy)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע בן לוי's 24 includes cases he compared to the explicit ones. רבי אלעזר counted only the clear cases.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מְדַמֵּה מִילְּתָא לְמִילְּתָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi compares one matter to another,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לָא מְדַמֵּה מִילְּתָא לְמִילְּתָא.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Elazar does not compare one matter to another.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מְדַמֵּה מִילְּתָא לְמִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different method of counting: analogy versus explicit text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both Sages count the same way, so 24 seems impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהושע בן לוי includes similar cases by analogy. רבי אלעזר does not.

steps.title: Do not take out a body for burial near the time of קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: Returning to our משנה about pallbearers, the גמרא brings a ברייתא. We should not take out a מת for burial close to the time of קריאת שמע, but once the funeral has started, they need not stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The pallbearers and their replacements.' The Rabbis taught: We do not take out the dead close to the time of קריאת שמע. And if they started, they do not stop.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the funeral laws of our משנה and brings a ברייתא about timing a burial so it does not clash with קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before a funeral begins, we plan it so people will not be pulled away from קריאת שמע. But if the procession has already started, we do not interrupt it. The people busy with the מת are exempt, as our משנה taught about pallbearers.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not take out the dead (for burial)
They do not stop or interrupt

phrases.english: The pallbearers and their replacements.
phrases.notes: A quote from our משנה, introducing the new topic.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
We do not take out the dead
close to the time of the recitation of Shema.
And if they started, they do not stop.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. It returns to the funeral laws of our משנה after the long side discussion about נידוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not begin a burial close to the time of קריאת שמע. If it has already begun, do not interrupt it.

steps.title: But רב יוסף was buried near the time of קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא with a real event. רב יוסף was taken out for burial close to the time of קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But they took out רב יוסף close to the time of קריאת שמע!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the rule by pointing to a known case where people did exactly what the ברייתא says not to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The funeral of רב יוסף was held close to קריאת שמע time. This seems to go against the ברייתא's rule. If the Sages allowed it, the rule seems to be in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (a word that opens a challenge)

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But they took out Rav Yosef
close to the time of the recitation of Shema!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי וְהָא רַב יוֹסֵף אַפְּקוּהוּ סָמוּךְ לִקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא of Step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule not to take out the dead close to קריאת שמע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A real event, the burial of רב יוסף, went against the rule.

steps.title: An important person is different
steps.stepSummary: The burial of an important person is an exception. In his honor, the funeral may be held even close to קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: An important person is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב יוסף's funeral was an exception because of his greatness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule stays in place. Honoring a great Torah scholar at his burial is important enough to allow an earlier funeral. That is why רב יוסף's case does not disprove the ברייתא.

phrases.english: An important person is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: An exception: special honor for an important person.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יוסף's funeral shows the rule is not binding.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule stands. An important person's burial is a special exception for his honor.

steps.title: How eulogizers say קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: Quoting our משנה about those before and after the bier, the גמרא brings a ברייתא. If the מת is in front of them, the eulogizers slip out one at a time to say קריאת שמע. If not, they sit and say it, while the mourner sits silently.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Those before the bier and those after the bier.' The Rabbis taught: People busy with a eulogy, while the dead lies before them, slip away one by one and recite. If the dead is not lying before them, they sit and recite, and he (the mourner) sits silently.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains how people at a eulogy fit in קריאת שמע, depending on whether the body is present.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the מת is present, they leave one at a time so the מת is never left without honor. When the מת is not present, they may all recite in place. The mourner stays silent because he is exempt, since he is still busy with his dead before the burial.
steps.confusionAlert: 'He' (וְהוּא) refers to the mourner, not one of the eulogizers. The mourner does not recite, because he is exempt.

phrases.english: Those before the bier and those after the bier.
phrases.notes: A quote from our משנה.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: Those involved in a eulogy,
when the dead is lying before them,
slip away one by one and recite (Shema).
If the dead is not lying before them,
they sit and recite,
and he (the mourner) sits silently.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁלִּפְנֵי הַמִּטָּה וְשֶׁלְּאַחַר הַמִּטָּה. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָעוֹסְקִים בְּהֶסְפֵּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next phrase of our משנה and brings a new ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the מת is present, eulogizers leave one at a time to recite. If not, they recite in place, and the mourner stays silent.

steps.title: The mourner accepts God's judgment while others pray
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. While the others stand for תפילה, the mourner stands and says a prayer of צידוק הדין, accepting God's judgment and asking for mercy.
steps.simpleTranslation: They stand and pray, and he stands and accepts the judgment upon himself, saying: 'Master of the worlds, I have sinned much before You, and You have not collected from me even one in a thousand. May it be Your will, ה׳ our God, that You close up our breaches and the breaches of all Your nation, the House of Israel, with mercy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא tells us what the mourner says while everyone else prays. He accepts God's judgment and asks for mercy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mourner does not say the regular תפילה, but he is not idle. He says words that justify God's judgment. He admits his sins are greater than what he has suffered, and he asks God to repair the 'breaches' (losses) of the Jewish people.

keyTerms.meaning: Accepts God's judgment as just (צידוק הדין)

phrases.english: They stand and pray,

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא עוֹמֵד וּמַצְדִּיק עָלָיו אֶת הַדִּין,
phrases.english: and he stands and accepts the judgment upon himself,
and says: "Master of the worlds,
I have sinned greatly before You,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא נִפְרַעְתָּ מִמֶּנִּי אֶחָד מִנִּי אֶלֶף,
phrases.english: and You have not collected from me even one in a thousand,
may it be Your will, ה׳ our God,
that You close up our breaches

phrases.aramaic: וּפִרְצוֹת כׇּל עַמְּךָ בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּרַחֲמִים״.
phrases.english: and the breaches of all Your nation, the House of Israel, with mercy."

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵם עוֹמְדִים וּמִתְפַּלְּלִין, וְהוּא עוֹמֵד וּמַצְדִּיק עָלָיו אֶת הַדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא from Step 35.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During the others' תפילה, the mourner says צידוק הדין with the text given.

steps.title: אביי objects: never open your mouth to the שטן
steps.stepSummary: אביי says a person should not say the line 'You have not collected even one in a thousand.' He bases this on ריש לקיש, and a teaching in the name of רבי יוסי, that one should never 'open his mouth to the שטן.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: A person should not say this. As רבי שמעון בן לקיש said, and so it was taught in the name of רבי יוסי: A person should never open his mouth to the שטן.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי criticizes one line of the mourner's prayer and says it should not be said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'You have not yet punished me for even a thousandth of my sins' suggests that more punishment is still owed. That invites more suffering. אביי's source is the principle that a person should never speak in a way that opens the door to harm.

keyTerms.meaning: A person should not open his mouth to the שטן (should not speak of possible harm)

steps.whatToRemember: Even in a sincere prayer, a person should avoid words that invite more suffering. This is 'never open your mouth to the שטן.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle, אל יפתח אדם פיו לשטן, is a well-known guideline for how we speak, especially in times of mourning or danger.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: לָא מִבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְאִינָשׁ לְמֵימַר הָכִי,
phrases.english: A person should not say this,
as Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said,
and so it was taught in the name of Rabbi Yosei:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם אַל יִפְתַּח אָדָם פִּיו לַשָּׂטָן.
phrases.english: A person should never open his mouth to the Satan.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לָא מִבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְאִינָשׁ לְמֵימַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to the wording of the mourner's prayer quoted in Step 36.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'You have not collected from me even one in a thousand'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase suggests more punishment is still due, and that invites harm. One should never open his mouth to the שטן.

steps.title: A verse showing that negative words about yourself can come true
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings a פסוק from ישעיה. The people said 'we were almost like סדום,' and the נביא then called them 'rulers of סדום.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said: What verse teaches this? It says, 'We were almost like סדום.' And what did the prophet answer them? 'Hear the word of ה׳, rulers of סדום.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a פסוק as the source for the idea from step 37. A person should not 'open his mouth to the שטן' by speaking badly about himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people said about themselves, 'we were almost like סדום.' Right after that, the נביא spoke to them as 'rulers of סדום.' Their own words were turned into reality, which proves it is dangerous to say such things.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the verse? (asking for the source)

steps.whatToRemember: Speaking negatively about yourself can 'invite' that very outcome. That is why אביי says not to say 'You have not collected even one in a thousand' in צידוק הדין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the section about the mourner's צידוק הדין. It explains why some wording is avoided in prayer.

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said: What is the verse?
phrases.notes: He's asking which פסוק teaches 'do not open your mouth to the שטן.'

phrases.english: As it says: 'We were almost like Sodom,'
phrases.notes: ישעיה א:ט. The people speak negatively about themselves.

phrases.english: What did the prophet answer them?
'Hear the word of God, rulers of Sodom.'
phrases.notes: ישעיה א:י. Their own words came true.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the verse that supports אביי's principle from step 37.
steps.raayaObject: The principle that one should never 'open his mouth to the שטן.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיה א:ט-י. 'Almost like סדום' is followed by 'rulers of סדום.'

steps.title: Reading the משנה: only if they can finish the whole שמע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about returning from a burial. It reads it as saying they start קריאת שמע only if they can finish all of it, not just one section or one verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They buried the dead and returned, etc.' If they can begin and finish all of it, yes. But if only one section or one verse, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to our משנה, which talks about people returning from a burial. It explains it to mean they start קריאת שמע only if they can finish the whole thing before reaching the line of comforters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'if they can begin and finish.' The גמרא first reads 'finish' as finishing the entire שמע. So finishing only one section or one verse would not be enough. This reading sets up the contradiction in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They buried the dead and returned

phrases.english: 'They buried the dead and returned, etc.'
phrases.notes: Quoting our משנה.

phrases.english: If they are able to begin and finish
all of it, yes (they should start),

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל פֶּרֶק אֶחָד אוֹ פָּסוּק אֶחָד — לָא.
phrases.english: but only one section or one verse, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, returning to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First reading: they start קריאת שמע only if they can finish the whole thing.

steps.title: A ברייתא says even one section or one verse is enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets a ברייתא against this reading. The ברייתא says they should start even if they can finish only one section or one verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they raised a contradiction: 'They buried the dead and returned. If they can begin and finish even one section or one verse...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading from step 39. It brings a ברייתא that says finishing even one section or one verse is enough to start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 39 said finishing one section or verse is not enough. The ברייתא says 'even' one section or verse is enough. These two statements seem to clash directly.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contrasted them (a contradiction between two sources)

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
'They buried the dead and returned,
if they are able to begin and finish

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ פֶּרֶק אֶחָד אוֹ פָּסוּק אֶחָד!
phrases.english: even one section or one verse!'
phrases.notes: This seems to be exactly the opposite of the inference just made.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the משנה given in step 39.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the משנה requires finishing the whole שמע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא openly says that finishing even one section or one verse is enough. That contradicts the claim that only the whole שמע counts.

steps.title: The משנה means the same thing: even one section or verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is saying the same thing as the ברייתא. If they can finish even one section or one verse before reaching the line of comforters, they start. If not, they do not start.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also what it is saying: If they can begin and finish even one section, or even one verse, before they reach the line, they should begin. And if not, they should not begin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by dropping the reading from step 39. The משנה, like the ברייתא, means that finishing even one section or one verse before reaching the line of comforters is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'begin and finish' in the משנה do not refer to the entire שמע. They mean finishing some complete unit before reaching the line of comforters, even one section or one verse. Now the משנה and the ברייתא agree.

keyTerms.meaning: This is also what it is saying
The line of people who comfort the mourner

steps.whatToRemember: Coming back from a burial, start קריאת שמע only if you can finish at least one section or one verse before reaching the line of comforters. If you can't, don't start.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא's first reading, that the whole שמע is required, is dropped here. The conclusion is that even one section or one verse is enough.

phrases.english: This is also what it (the Mishnah) is saying:
If they are able to begin and finish

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ פֶּרֶק אֶחָד אוֹ אֲפִילּוּ פָּסוּק אֶחָד
phrases.english: even one section, or even one verse,
before they reach the line (of comforters), they should begin,
and if not, they should not begin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from step 40 by rereading the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה so it matches the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה requires finishing the entire שמע before reaching the line.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה also means that finishing even one section or one verse before reaching the line is enough.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Start קריאת שמע only if you can finish at least one section or one verse before reaching the line of comforters.
